title: Curve projective dense completion
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a separated finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with $\dim X\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. There exist a projective $k$-scheme $C$ [def-kun-projective] of dimension at most one and an open immersion $a:X\to C$ [def-weil-open-immersion] whose image is dense and scheme-theoretically dense (the map $\mathcal O_C\to a_*\mathcal O_X$ is injective), with complement a finite set of closed points. If $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], $C$ can be taken reduced. If $X$ is empty, $C$ can be empty.

source.place: Tag 0BXV, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion; proof: scheme-theoretic closure, whose reduction agrees over reduced X

proof.text: Finite type over Spec k makes X Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Every morphism from a Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact (Mathlib quasiCompact_of_noetherianSpace_source, implementing [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]). Apply [lem-sc-dim-one-quasi-projective] to obtain a closed immersion i into U and an open immersion j from U into a finite projective space, over k. Their composite h is a quasi-compact immersion.

source.place: Tag 0BXV, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion; proof: scheme-theoretic closure, whose reduction agrees over reduced X

proof.text: Let C=h.image, a=h.toImage, and let g be h.imageι followed by the projective-space structure map. These are the constructed image, closed inclusion, and factor map of [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], a is an open immersion. Mathlib gives IsDominant a and the proved source ker_toImage instance gives IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant a; app_injective supplies injectivity on all rings of sections. The closed inclusion exhibits [def-kun-projective], and associativity and toImage_imageι give a composed with g equal to the original structure map.

source.place: Tag 0BXV, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion; proof: scheme-theoretic closure, whose reduction agrees over reduced X

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper] and [def-weil-proper-morphism], g is proper and finite type. Thus C is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-dimension-comparison] to a.opensRange. The open embedding identifies its dimension with dim X, giving dim C at most dim X at most one. This reuses the complete existing topologicalKrullDim_le_of_dense rather than rebuilding the generic residue-field comparison.

source.place: Tag 0BXV, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion; proof: scheme-theoretic closure, whose reduction agrees over reduced X

proof.text: Put E=C minus range(a), a closed subset. Noetherianity and [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], together with [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober], give a maximal generalization eta of every c in E; the source helper isClosed_univ.exists_maximal_specializes supplies it. Every such eta belongs to the dense open image, by the source helper mem_of_dense_of_forall_specializes_eq (finite component argument as in the dense-open comparison proof). Thus each specialization chain in E extends in C by a point outside E. The proved topologicalKrullDim_lt_of_forall_exists_specializes applies with the whole space as Z and d=1: dim C at most 1 is strictly less than 2, so dim E is strictly less than 1, hence at most zero by ENat.WithBot.lt_add_one_iff. Now [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-closed-finite] gives E finite and all its points closed in C. All arguments allow empty, reducible and mixed-dimensional C.

source.place: Tag 0BXV, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion; proof: scheme-theoretic closure, whose reduction agrees over reduced X

proof.text: If X is reduced, apply IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.isReduced a: injectivity on rings of sections embeds every section ring of C into a reduced section ring of X, hence it is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

source.place: Tag 0BXV, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion; proof: scheme-theoretic closure, whose reduction agrees over reduced X

proof.text: If X is empty, range a is empty, and density implies every point of C lies in the closure of the empty set, an impossibility. Thus C is empty.

source.place: Tag 0BXV, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion; proof: scheme-theoretic closure, whose reduction agrees over reduced X

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BXV, lemma-dim-1-projective-completion; scheme-theoretic closure retained, dimension comparison reused from the proved DenseCompactification theorem, and finite boundary proved by specialization-chain extension and the proved zero-dimensional closed-subset finiteness theorem. Lean implementation U9.

lean.statement: theorem exists_projective_dense_completion_of_dim_le_one {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) : ∃ (C : Scheme.{u}) (g : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (a : X ⟶ C), IsHProjective g ∧ topologicalKrullDim C ≤ 1 ∧ IsOpenImmersion a ∧ a ≫ g = X ↘ Spec (.of k) ∧ DenseRange a ∧ (∀ U : C.Opens, Function.Injective (a.app U)) ∧ (Set.range a)ᶜ.Finite ∧ (∀ c : C, c ∉ Set.range a → IsClosed ({c} : Set C)) ∧ (IsReduced X → IsReduced C) ∧ (IsEmpty X → IsEmpty C)
